rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only single-profile model provides a usable performance floor. This configuration tests the most basic RNA representation, PCA, without image features, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion, giving a clean reference point for later comparisons with learned RNA encoders, multiprofile settings, image-only models, and multimodal fusion. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it is simple, low-confounding, and establishes an anchor without assuming that more complex multimodal models will be better.

Only one experiment is completed, so evidence is sparse: RNA-only single-profile PCA gives moderate accuracy and F1, but it does not tell whether the image modality contains useful signal. config_010 is a minimal image-only baseline with single profile, ResNet50, and no aggregation or fusion, so it cleanly tests image representation and provides a second unimodal reference. This is the best next experiment under a limited budget because it avoids assuming that multimodal or multiprofile models will help, and it will clarify whether later effort should focus on image, RNA, or fusion.

Existing evidence: RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile in both accuracy and F1, but it is still unclear whether using multiple profiles with simple aggregation improves the RNA representation. config_002 tests this by keeping the same PCA RNA encoder and adding multiprofile with avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect without introducing a new encoder or fusion. It is the best next budget use because it exploits the currently strongest direction, may improve validation accuracy, and will determine whether multiprofile RNA is worth extending to more complex aggregations or multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is config_002, where multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool reaches 0.591 accuracy and 0.573 F1, clearly above single-profile RNA and far above image-only ResNet50. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation improves over avgpool for this promising RNA multiprofile setting. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, keeping model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, so it cleanly isolates the aggregation effect. This is a high-value exploitation step: it may directly improve performance and also tells whether transformer aggregation is worth carrying into later multimodal experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool reaches 0.591 accuracy, clearly above singleprofile PCA and multiprofile transformer, while image-only ResNet is weak. This suggests the next informative step is to test whether a learned RNA representation improves on PCA under the already-promising multiprofile avgpool setting. config_005 isolates the RNA encoder choice by changing only from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200, making it a focused exploitation of the current best direction and a useful check before adding multimodal fusion complexity.

RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is currently the strongest direction, with scvi_n200 reaching 0.650 acc / 0.628 F1 and outperforming pca_n2000 multiprofile avgpool (0.591 / 0.573) and single-profile PCA (0.485 / 0.464); avgpool also beat transformer for PCA. The key uncertainty is whether scvi_n200 is specifically better or whether another learned RNA encoder can match it under the same favorable profile and aggregation. config_008 tests scgpt with multiprofile avgpool, changing only the RNA encoder from the current best. This is a clean, high-information exploitation of the promising RNA-only pipeline, helps decide the best representation before adding image/fusion, and avoids prematurely testing multimodal configurations while image-only evidence remains weak.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, reaching 0.650 validation accuracy and 0.628 F1, while multiprofile avgpool also clearly helped PCA. The key uncertainty is whether scvi_n200’s performance depends on multiprofile aggregation or would be competitive as a simpler single-profile model. config_004 tests single-profile scvi_n200, directly isolating the profile-setting effect for the most promising RNA encoder without introducing image or fusion variables. This exploits the best-known representation while reducing uncertainty about whether added multiprofile complexity is necessary, making it a high-information next experiment under a limited budget.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile avgpool with scvi_n200 is strong, but image-only evidence is sparse: only ResNet50 singleprofile was tested and performed poorly. This experiment tests whether a stronger ImageNet ViT-L image encoder yields useful image-only signal, isolating representation while keeping the profile setting fixed. It is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about whether the image modality is worth pursuing before multimodal fusion, avoids confounding encoder, profile, and fusion changes, and will guide whether remaining experiments should target image/multimodal settings or focus on RNA.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), showing that multiprofile RNA representation is promising. However, aggregation is still uncertain: avgpool beat transformer for PCA multiprofile, but transformer has not been tested with the best scvi_n200 multiprofile setting. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer in the leading RNA-only setting, directly testing whether profile interactions improve the strongest current model. This is a high-value next experiment because it exploits the best evidence while isolating an important design choice before moving to multimodal settings, where image and fusion changes would confound the interpretation.

RNA-only multiprofile models, especially scvi_n200 with avgpool/transformer, are currently strongest, showing that multiprofile aggregation can help. In contrast, both image-only single-profile encoders are weak (ResNet50 ~0.208, ViT-L ~0.227), and no image-only multiprofile result is available. config_014 tests whether the better single-profile image encoder (ViT-L) improves under multiprofile avgpool aggregation, using a clean one-factor extension from config_013. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces key uncertainty about whether the image modality has any usable signal before spending experiments on multimodal fusion; if image-only multiprofile remains weak, multimodal models are less likely to help, while if it improves, a subsequent multimodal scvi+ViT experiment becomes much more interpretable.
